# Architecture Overview — Fields Behavior Candidates and Before-use Cycle Checks

> architecture-overview · [m2ux/workflow-server#1692](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1692) · 2026-11-11

## Summary

The shared skill checker, [check_skill_files.py](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/6fce88bdc343d55093d762daecc6557f1a7d5401/skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py#L1-L120), gains three checks over a skill's Markdown: execution written inside a declared Fields section, Fields prose that reads as behavior, and cycles among explicit "read this before that" requirements. Two are failing finding kinds and one is a non-failing review candidate. Work Planner's [rules.json](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/6fce88bdc343d55093d762daecc6557f1a7d5401/skills/work-planner/rules.json#L9-L16) names the new kinds as the operations deciding three of its house rules.

## Structure

All production code lands in one file, the checker. Its command entry `main` runs the per-file `check`, then the skill-wide checks. The change adds one per-file check (`fields_steps`), one skill-wide failing check (`before_use_findings`) and one skill-wide candidate pass (`fields_candidates`). The two Fields checks share `contract_sections`. A *contract section* is the level-2 heading a skill's `structure.json` declares under `contracts` (Fields, for every Work Planner modes, protocols and artifacts file). `undecided_rules` is untouched. It reads each guide's `rules.json` and accepts only the kind names listed in `OPERATIONS`, which now holds the new kinds.

```mermaid
---
title: Components — check_skill_files.py
---
flowchart LR
    CLI([skill author / CI])

    subgraph PerFile [Per-file check]
        Check[check]
        Steps[fields_steps]
    end

    subgraph Fields [Fields candidates]
        Cand[fields_candidates]
        Clauses[behavior_clauses]
    end

    Sections[contract_sections]

    subgraph Order [Before-use ordering]
        Findings[before_use_findings]
        Graph[before_use_graph]
        Cycles[before_use_cycles]
    end

    Rules[undecided_rules]

    CLI -->|roots| Main[main]
    Main -->|each file| Check
    Check -->|Fields execution| Steps
    Steps -->|section spans| Sections
    Main -->|each file| Cand
    Cand -->|section spans| Sections
    Cand -->|field prose| Clauses
    Main -->|all files| Findings
    Findings -->|build graph| Graph
    Findings -->|find cycles| Cycles
    Main -->|each guide| Rules

    style Steps fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#2e7d32
    style Sections fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#2e7d32
    style Cand fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#2e7d32
    style Clauses fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#2e7d32
    style Findings fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#2e7d32
    style Graph fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#2e7d32
    style Cycles fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#2e7d32
    style Main fill:#fff3e0,stroke:#ef6c00
    style Check fill:#fff3e0,stroke:#ef6c00
    style Rules fill:#f5f5f5,stroke:#9e9e9e
```

Green is added, orange is altered, grey is untouched. Edges are the measured call relationships of `main`, `check`, `fields_candidates` and `before_use_findings`.

### Per-file check

- **check.**
  Runs every per-file check and records each as a finding. It now also runs `fields_steps` and reports each hit as `executable step in Fields` ([L917-L918](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/6fce88bdc343d55093d762daecc6557f1a7d5401/skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py#L917-L918)).
- **fields_steps.**
  Flags execution inside a contract section: a numbered list step, a numbered heading, or a call verb (`Run`, plus the declared `calls` verbs such as `Apply` and `Follow`) right before a link resolving to an operation or command. Fenced text and HTML invocations are skipped, since other checks own them.

### Fields candidates

- **fields_candidates.**
  For each level-3 field under a contract section, gathers behavior clauses. When at least one clause has an actor or an instruction, and the clauses span two or more behavior kinds, it emits a `Fields behavior candidate`. That candidate carries each clause's line and kinds, plus the file's `Operations` section as the possible owner.
- **behavior_clauses.**
  Splits a field's prose into sentences and tags them with the kinds `acquire`, `write`, `route` and `transition`. It uses word lists (`BEHAVIORS`), actor nouns (`ACTORS`), passive participles and transition verbs. Tables, headings, fences and invocations are not read.

### Before-use ordering

- **before_use_findings.**
  Builds the graph from every checked Markdown file, finds its cycles and reports each as one `before-use cycle` finding, naming every node and the line of the requirement leaving it.
- **before_use_graph.**
  A node is a file plus an optional heading anchor. An edge is a `Requirement` (source line, target file and anchor, condition) that `requirements` extracts. Only three forms count: a `Read [x] first.` or `Read [x] before ….` sentence, a link in a `## Prerequisites` section, and a link to a declared `preamble` file in the file introduction. `read_span` limits a node's edges to what its read takes: the whole file, or one heading's section plus the file introduction.
- **before_use_cycles.**
  Tarjan's strongly-connected-components search (inner `connect`), then a breadth-first walk inside each component, gives the shortest closed witness from its first node back to itself.

## Behaviour

Three flows run through the change: Fields execution inside the per-file check, the before-use cycle check and the Fields candidate pass. The last two run once per command after the per-file checks.

### Fields Execution

Each file `check` reads with a declared contract section starts it. Each executable line yields one failing finding.

```mermaid
---
title: Sequence — Fields Execution
---
sequenceDiagram
    participant Check as check
    participant Steps as fields_steps
    participant Sections as contract_sections
    participant Target as operation_target / command_target
    participant Contract as contract

    Check->>Steps: lines, headings, structure entry
    Steps->>Sections: contract section spans
    Sections-->>Steps: (start, end) per section
    Steps->>Target: link after a call verb
    Target->>Contract: target file's declared structure
    Contract-->>Target: operations / commands
    Target-->>Steps: operation or command, or none
    Steps-->>Check: (line, detail)
    Check->>Check: report "executable step in Fields"
```

- **Section span.**
  The span runs from the declared level-2 heading to the next heading of equal or higher level. A file whose structure declares no `contracts` yields no span.
- **Call resolution.**
  A link counts only when it resolves to an operation or a command. A definition link to an operation with no call verb before it is not execution.

### Before-use Cycle

`main` runs this flow once over every file under the named roots. It yields zero or more `before-use cycle` findings, and any finding makes the command exit 1.

```mermaid
---
title: Sequence — Before-use Cycle
---
sequenceDiagram
    participant Main as main
    participant Findings as before_use_findings
    participant Graph as before_use_graph
    participant Span as read_span
    participant Cycles as before_use_cycles
    participant Named as named

    Main->>Findings: files, declared structures
    Findings->>Graph: whole-file nodes
    loop each pending node
        Graph->>Graph: requirements(file) once per file
        Graph->>Span: node's read span
        Span-->>Graph: line set
        Graph->>Graph: keep edges in span, queue targets
    end
    Graph-->>Findings: node → requirements
    Findings->>Cycles: graph
    Cycles->>Cycles: connect (strong components)
    Cycles-->>Findings: closed witnesses
    Findings->>Named: label each node
    Named-->>Findings: skill-relative name
    Findings-->>Main: "before-use cycle" findings
```

- **Bounded read.**
  A heading read pulls in its own section's and the introduction's requirements, not its siblings'. So a diamond of requirements or a sibling section's requirement is not a cycle.
- **What imposes no order.**
  Ordinary links, field references, execution calls (retried or not) and fenced specimen text create no edge.

### Fields Candidate

`main` runs this flow per file whose structure declares `contracts`. It yields candidates that print but never change the exit status.

```mermaid
---
title: Sequence — Fields Candidate
---
sequenceDiagram
    participant Main as main
    participant Cand as fields_candidates
    participant Contract as contract
    participant Sections as contract_sections
    participant Clauses as behavior_clauses

    Main->>Cand: path, root, declared structures
    Cand->>Contract: file's structure entry
    Contract-->>Cand: entry with "contracts"
    Cand->>Sections: contract section spans
    Sections-->>Cand: spans
    loop each level-3 field
        Cand->>Clauses: field span
        Clauses-->>Cand: (line, sentence, agentive, kinds)
    end
    Cand-->>Main: "Fields behavior candidate" rows
```

- **Threshold.**
  At least one agentive clause, plus two or more distinct kinds across the field. A conditional invariant names no actor, so it stays clear.
- **Output.**
  `main` prints candidates after findings and adds `, N review candidates` to the summary line. The exit code depends on findings alone.

## What Changed

### Checker

- **Finding kinds.**
  `KINDS` adds `executable step in Fields` and `before-use cycle`. The new `CANDIDATES` tuple holds `Fields behavior candidate`, and `OPERATIONS` is now `KINDS + CANDIDATES + ('review',)`, so `rules.json` can name a candidate.
- **Command.**
  `main` runs the before-use and candidate passes after the per-file checks and reports candidates separately from findings.
- **Module docstring.**
  States the before-use relation and the Fields boundary ([L73-L88](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/6fce88bdc343d55093d762daecc6557f1a7d5401/skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py#L73-L88)).

### Work Planner rules

- **rules.json.**
  `solid/callable-transformations` is decided by `executable step in Fields`, `solid/boundary-review` by `Fields behavior candidate`, and `solid/before-use-ordering` by `before-use cycle`, each still alongside `review`.

### Tests

- **New suites.**
  `FieldsBoundary`, `BeforeUseOrdering` and `InstalledWorkPlannerModel`, plus the pinned 756aaf9 Prerequisites inventory fixture, which the measured 13-artifact cycle test reads.

The change-by-change listing is the pull request's [Changes](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1692) section.

## Reading Order

1. **[check_skill_files.py — kinds](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/6fce88bdc343d55093d762daecc6557f1a7d5401/skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py#L177-L204)**: the new finding and candidate names, and how `rules.json` may cite them.
2. **[check_skill_files.py — main](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/6fce88bdc343d55093d762daecc6557f1a7d5401/skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py#L1759-L1818)**: where the two skill-wide passes run and how candidates leave the exit code alone.
3. **[check_skill_files.py — Fields checks](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/6fce88bdc343d55093d762daecc6557f1a7d5401/skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py#L1474-L1604)**: `contract_sections`, `fields_steps`, the behavior vocabularies, `behavior_clauses` and `fields_candidates`.
4. **[check_skill_files.py — before-use ordering](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/6fce88bdc343d55093d762daecc6557f1a7d5401/skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py#L1607-L1756)**: `BEFORE_USE`, `Requirement`, `requirements`, `read_span`, `before_use_graph`, `before_use_cycles` and `before_use_findings`.
5. **[rules.json](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/6fce88bdc343d55093d762daecc6557f1a7d5401/skills/work-planner/rules.json#L9-L16)**: the three rules the new kinds decide.
6. **[test_check_skill_files.py](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/6fce88bdc343d55093d762daecc6557f1a7d5401/skills/test/test_check_skill_files.py#L2317-L2641)**: the positive cases and controls for each check, and the installed-model assertions.

## Risks and Watch Points

- **Lexical candidate test.**
  `behavior_clauses` decides by word lists, so a paraphrase outside `BEHAVIORS` or `ACTORS` is missed, and a value field using those words can be flagged. Candidates fail nothing, which bounds the cost. Calibration over the 518 W02 ledger fields is in the PR's T2.
- **Graph size from `--compare`-less runs.**
  `before_use_graph` follows requirement targets outside the named roots when links point there (`path.parent / name`). A broken or external relative link becomes a node with an empty read span, not an error.
- **Installed model pinned in tests.**
  `InstalledWorkPlannerModel` asserts the graph equals the 38 audited requirements ([L2620](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/6fce88bdc343d55093d762daecc6557f1a7d5401/skills/test/test_check_skill_files.py#L2620)). Any later Work Planner edit adding a `Read … first.` sentence or Prerequisites link must update that set.
- **Graph limits.**
  `requirements` and `behavior_clauses` sit in no indexed process. Their places in the flows above come from symbol-context call edges, not process traces.

## References

- **R1.** [Work item w37](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/87e80b73f735de102a5775f8d9d8f619125eb05e/artifacts/planning/2026-11-11-1615-i17-e02-w37-detect-fields-behavior-and/w37.md): declared components and observing validation.
- **R2.** [Validation](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/87e80b73f735de102a5775f8d9d8f619125eb05e/artifacts/planning/2026-11-11-1615-i17-e02-w37-detect-fields-behavior-and/validation.md): diagnostics, tests, base control and calibration.
- **R3.** [Graph measurements](graph-measurements.md): exact-head change surface, symbol contexts and flow traces behind the diagrams.
